prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a sideswipe while changing lanes claim. Injury: wrist fracture. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1306; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Reviewed the first notice of loss for the sideswipe collision during a lane change. Insured reports the other vehicle drifted into their lane on the highway and contact occurred at the rear quarter panel. Police report requested. Scene photos from the insured are on file and show scraping along the driver side. Claimant reported a wrist fracture at the scene and was transported by ambulance.

Entry 2: Spoke with the insured for a recorded statement. Insured confirms they checked mirrors and signaled before moving over but acknowledges their view of the adjacent lane was partially blocked by a truck. Witness contact information noted from the police report and a follow-up call was scheduled. Liability currently appears disputed, with preliminary fault leaning toward the other driver.

Entry 3: Received notice that the claimant is represented by counsel. All further communication regarding the bodily injury claim will be routed through the attorney's office. Requested medical authorization and itemized records for the wrist fracture treatment, including orthopedic consultation notes and surgical records if applicable. Reserve placed on the bodily injury coverage pending documentation.

Entry 4: Obtained the vehicle damage appraisal for the claimant's vehicle and the insured's vehicle. Repair estimates reviewed and found consistent with the photographed damage. Rental coverage confirmed for the insured. Dashcam footage from a nearby vehicle has been requested through the witness and may help resolve the lane position question.

Entry 5: Received a letter of representation and a demand package from the claimant's attorney, which is under review. Medical bills and wage loss documentation are still incomplete. Scheduled an internal file review with the supervisor to assess liability allocation and settlement authority. Next step is to follow up on the outstanding records and the dashcam request before responding to the demand.
